intended_object: The normalized Atkin–Lehner involution 𝒲_Q, for an exact divisor Q ∥ N, acting on the space S_k(N, 1) of cusp forms of level N with trivial nebentypus (identified with S_k(Γ₀(N))). This is inferred from the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation:
The body conjugates the library's normalized Atkin–Lehner operator on S_k(Γ₀(N)) by the linear equivalence `cuspFormCharSpaceOneEquiv`. That equivalence identifies the χ = 1 eigenspace inside S_k(Γ₁(N)) with S_k(Γ₀(N)): one direction promotes the form to Γ₀(N), the other restricts it to Γ₁(N).

The underlying operator is `atkinLehnerNormalizer Q k • (f ↦ f ∣[k] W_Q)`, where W_Q is an Atkin–Lehner matrix of determinant Q. Its coercion lemma gives the scalar as (√Q)^(2−k). Mathlib's slash action carries a factor det^(k−1), so the result is the standard Q^{k/2}(cz+d)^{−k} f(W_Q z), which is the usual involutive normalization. On Γ₀(N), the operator does not depend on which Atkin–Lehner matrix is chosen.

So on S_k(N, 1) the definition is exactly the classical 𝒲_Q, and the docstring describes it accurately. Restricting to trivial nebentypus is not a narrowing. As the module documentation notes, for general χ the operator W_Q does not preserve S_k(N, χ): it changes the Q-part of the character. Mathlib has no Atkin–Lehner operators.
